comment: Storage path families: the single source of truth for storage.rules (plans/firestore-rules §3.2, §4.11, T16). Every object path belongs to exactly one family. `read`/`write` say what the family grants: `signedIn` and `none` are generic (the generated blocks in storage.rules apply them, no rule edit needed), `block` means the family's own match blocks (`matchBlocks`) decide. security/generate_storage.js renders the generated section of storage.rules from this file; security/check_rules_exceptions.js approves exactly the `matchBlocks` listed here. `migrate` marks the legacy prefixes M8 (scripts/firestore_admin/migrations/2026-11-05_migrate_storage_legacy.js) moves, and where to: `<prefix>/<rest>` becomes groups/{g}/apps/{appId}/{folder}/<rest>, the folder the app's ScopedStorage writes today, so a migrated file sits exactly where a new upload would.

group_apps.what: Group-scoped app files (ScopedStorage). The tenant rule: the caller's access index must list the path's group (ACTIVE, not denied), and an entitlement for the path's app narrows it. Members read; base tier creates and edits/deletes its own files; :edit/:admin edit any; guests (:guest) create, read and edit only their own, and only in the app's guestWritableFolders, within its guestUploadLimits (size and content type) where it has them. Metadata groupId/appId must equal the path; creatorId is the uploader and can't be forged. Files in an app's retainedFolders are kept for the record: once uploaded, no client deletes, overwrites or changes one (only the Admin SDK removes it). Platform admins (ACTIVE) read (EX-ADMIN-1). No public branch (D2).
group_apps.why: The generic tenant rule (plan 2.4, 4.11); the Storage counterpart of firestore.rules' inTenant() && detail(). retainedFolders is the Storage side of blockDelete, for the attachments regulated records point at.

group_logo.what: Group logos set before versioning (new ones go to group_logo_versions). Signed-in read; no client write: the groupAdminSetLogo callable (functions/_group_logo.js, used by Group Admin and the Groups app) checks the caller (the group's admins, {g}:groups:admin, ACTIVE platform admins and developers; a frozen group only platform admins) and normalizes the image.
group_logo.why: Platform branding outside the app hierarchy, shown in group pickers and invitations. One server write path keeps every logo change on the audit trail and every stored logo a re-encoded image.

group_logo_versions.what: Every group logo ever set: groups/{groupId}/logos/{version}/ holds logo.jpg, logo_thumb.png and logo_print.png, written by groupAdminSetLogo (functions/_group_logo.js) to a new version folder each time, with a Storage precondition that refuses to overwrite. The group doc's logoUrl, logoThumbnailUrl and logoPrintUrl name the current version; earlier versions stay. Signed-in read, no client write.
group_logo_versions.why: Regulated groups keep every logo they have shown: a change adds a version and the groups doc's audit trail records which one was current, so nothing is overwritten or lost.

group_logo_renditions.what: Thumbnails and print copies of the logos set before versioning (by groupAdminSetLogo, or generateGroupLogoThumbnail in functions/app_icons.js). Signed-in read, no client write.

published.what: The public namespace (D2): published/{sourceGroupId}/{appId}/{collection}/{sourceId}/{file}, copies of the files of published docs (listing photos, public Storage app files). Signed-in read; no client write: functions/public_namespace.js (publicPublish/publicUnpublish and the re-sync trigger) is the only writer, through the Admin SDK.
published.why: Cross-group public files leave the tenant paths entirely (plan 2.7): no rule under groups/ grants another group anything.

app_icons.what: Platform app icons (App Manager). Signed-in read; ACTIVE platform admins and developers write.
app_icons.why: The global app catalog's icons, no tenant (plan 3.2: admin/developer).

app_icons_thumbs.what: App icon thumbnails written by functions/app_icons.js. Signed-in read, no client write.

app_screenshots.what: App store screenshots, app_screenshots/{appId}/{scene}_{formFactor}_{theme}.png, captured from the Sunnyside demo group by scripts/app_screenshots/ and listed in apps/{appId}.screenshots. Signed-in read; no client write: scripts/app_screenshots/publish.js (Admin SDK) is the only writer.
app_screenshots.why: Platform catalog assets with no tenant, like app icons (plans/add-apps/OVERVIEW.md 5.5).

profile_pictures.what: Profile pictures, keyed per uid: profile_pictures/{uid}/{file} is written only by that uid and read by the owner, users who share a group with them, and ACTIVE platform admins. Legacy flat profile_pictures/{file} objects are read-only (signed in).
profile_pictures.why: A user's picture is personal, not any one group's, so it can't be the tenant rule; co-member read needs the subject's access index (a second firestore.get). The app shows pictures through the token URL stored in users/{uid}.profilePictureUrl, so reads through the rules are rare.

chat_images.what: Legacy chat images (before groups/{g}/apps/chat/images). Signed-in read, no writes; archive later.
chat_images.why: Kept read-only for old messages (plan 3.2); 2 objects.

server_only.what: Server-only data: the data warehouse's private files and Blue Ji's docs corpus. No client access.
server_only.why: Written and read only through the Admin SDK (plan 3.2).

legacy_users.why: Pre-ScopedStorage data; M8 moves it into groups/{g}/apps/storage/files/{uid}/… and rewrites files.downloadUrl.

legacy_public.why: Pre-ScopedStorage data; M8 migrates it (public copies go to published/ through T27, not back here).

legacy_gallery_photos.why: Pre-ScopedStorage data; M8 migrates it. gallery_screen.dart deletes through refFromURL, which fails once enforced until migrated.

legacy_bug_reports_media.what: Legacy Improve Apps bug report attachments.

legacy_feature_request_media.what: Legacy Improve Apps feature request attachments.

removed_apps.what: Data of apps removed from the repo (Recorder, Video Editor). No client access; archive, then delete.
removed_apps.why: No client reads or writes these any more (plan 3.2).

unmatched.what: Every path no other family claims (including other paths under groups/{g}/). Denied.
unmatched.why: Default deny: a new prefix needs a family here before clients can use it.
